prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1392; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was struck from behind while stopped at a red light. Claimant reports neck and back pain at the scene and was transported by ambulance for evaluation. No attorney on file. Initial contact made by phone with the claimant, who is cooperative and provided the police report number.

Entry 2: Obtained the responding officer's report, which notes both vehicles drivable after the impact and no airbag deployment. Photos of rear bumper damage to the claimant's vehicle received and reviewed. Estimate requested from the body shop. Claimant confirmed she is seeing her primary care physician for neck and lower back strain and has been advised to keep all treatment records.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant regarding her recovery. She reports stiffness in the neck, limited rotation when checking traffic, and intermittent lower back pain that worsens after sitting for long periods. She is not working full duty and has asked about rental coverage. Explained rental benefits under the policy and set up a rental reservation pending review of the vehicle's repair timeline.

Entry 4: Received the repair estimate and medical records summary from the claimant's physician. Diagnosis is cervical and lumbar strain with a recommended course of physical therapy. No fractures or imaging-confirmed disc injury noted at this time. Reviewed liability with the at-fault driver's carrier, who has accepted fault for the rear impact. Subrogation file opened.

Entry 5: Followed up with the claimant to confirm she has started physical therapy and that the rental vehicle is meeting her needs. She asked whether she should have an attorney review the claim; advised her that she is free to do so and that we will continue to communicate directly with her in the meantime. Diary set for follow-up after the next physical therapy progress report.
